ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, a point A is selected on the opposite side of the river. Then, on this side of the river, points B and C are chosen such that $AB \perp BC$. Another point E is selected such that $EC \perp BC$, and the line of sight determines that BC and AE intersect at point D. At this moment, it is measured that $BD=120\,m$, $DC=60\,m$, and $EC=50\,m$. What is the distance between the two sides of the river, that is, the length of AB?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB\perp BC$, $EC\perp BC$,\\
$\therefore AB\parallel CE$\\
$\therefore \triangle ABD\sim \triangle ECD$\\
$\therefore \frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{EC}$\\
Given $BD=120m$, $DC=60m$, $EC=50m$,\\
$\therefore AB=\frac{BD\cdot EC}{DC}=\frac{120\times 50}{60}=\boxed{100}m$
